reason: Brad, 2026-10-03: ThriftyCrew is being decommissioned, stop the alerts from firing. This silences the inbox only: send-alert.ps1 still writes every alert to triage-queue.json, but nothing reads that queue now (grocery-alert-triage and every TC task were disabled the same day). No expiry on purpose: decom has no start date yet, and an expiring mute would resume mail by itself. Plan: design/PLAN-decom-2026-10-03.md.
how_to_resume_email: Set muted to false (keep the file so the mute periods stay on the record). No code change or redeploy needed - send-alert.ps1 reads it on every call.
covers: Every caller of grocery/send-alert.ps1 in this checkout, including -Force, hand runs, Claude sessions, git hooks and the shared knowledge store's recall-sleep.py (it runs this checkout's send-alert.ps1)
A worktree reads its OWN copy of this file, so a worktree made before this commit landed still mails until it is rebased
not_covered_by_this_file: The Cloudflare Worker (feed.thriftycrew.com): /ops-alert relay (only the dispatch-only GitHub workflows call it), the box-heartbeat cron (never configured: no BOX_KV binding, ops/out/boot-watch-state.json first_configured_utc null), and /submit + /notify, which are member-facing mail, not alerts
GitHub's own workflow-failure emails (all three workflows are workflow_dispatch-only, so none run on a clock)
Ghost staff notification emails (new member, paid signup, cancellation) and Stripe emails: account settings in those services, not repo code
Windows toasts and Claude desktop notifications from a live session
